assessments.technical_explanation: The scanner flagged environment-variable serialization at the point where the build script reads TAURI_UPDATER_PUBLIC_KEY and passes it into a config generator. Reviewing the actual data flow: the value read is a Tauri updater signing PUBLIC key, which by design is distributed to clients and embedded in the shipped app to verify update signatures — it is not a credential or secret. The script validates the value's structure, embeds it only in a locally generated updater configuration file within the repository, and emits a release tag. There is no network transmission of environment contents, no inclusion of other environment variables, no obfuscation, and no execution path beyond an explicit developer/CI invocation gated on being run as the main module. This matches the stated purpose of preparing signed auto-update configuration for the project's Windows releases. The 'serialize-environment' heuristic is a candidate-locating signal only; the demonstrated data flow shows no secret handling and no exfiltration.
assessments.layman_explanation: A scanner noticed the script takes information from a system environment variable and wrote it into a file, which can sometimes indicate secret theft. Here, the value is a public signing key — a piece of information that is deliberately shared with users so their app can verify that updates genuinely come from the project. It is written only into a local build configuration file, never sent anywhere over the network. This is a normal, expected step for setting up secure automatic updates.
assessments.developer_action: none
